short: Someone took over my phone number
title: My phone lost signal and someone has my number: what you can do now
pageTitle: My phone lost signal and someone has my number: what you can do now | Spamlock
description: Phone suddenly has no signal and someone else has your number (SIM swap)? Steps you can take now: call your provider, your bank, and protect your email.
answer: Call your mobile provider from another phone and ask for your number back. Then change your email password and call your bank.
stepsTitle: Steps you can take if someone took over your phone number

steps.title: Call your mobile provider
steps.text: From another phone. Ask them to give your number back.

steps.title: Change your email password
steps.text: Thieves use your number to get sign-in codes.

steps.title: Call your bank
steps.text: On the number on your card, not one from a message. You can ask them to check for payments you didn’t make.

steps.title: Get codes from an app, not by text
steps.text: In each account’s security settings, choose an authenticator app instead of text messages. Then sign-in codes don’t go to your number.

steps.title: Ask for a lock on your number
steps.text: Ask your provider for a number lock or PIN, if they offer it. Then no one can move your number again without it.

steps.title: Report it
steps.text: It helps stop others being caught. Outside the US and UK, you can report it to your local police.

app.title: This guide is in the Spamlock app
app.text: Mark each step as done as you go.
